dataset_verification.provenance: De-identified daily census telemetry generated from tertiary hospital operational distributions. Zero PHI.

benchmark_inconsistency_investigation.mathematical_explanation: During the stable summer/autumn training period, stationary 7-day day-of-week seasonality dominated (r7=0.51), allowing Seasonal Naive to outperform Persistence across Folds 1-3. However, during the late-year test period (Nov-Dec), a sharp non-stationary winter surge occurred: mean arrivals jumped from 173 to 186 and variance surged by 53%. Day-of-week seasonality broke down (r7 turned negative to -0.08), causing Seasonal Naive (t-7) to lag behind level shifts by a full week (MAE 27.13). Conversely, Persistence (t-1) immediately absorbed the regime shift on the next day (MAE 21.38, r1=+0.48).

Ridge_vs_Random_Forest.conclusion: No statistically significant difference between Ridge and Random Forest (p > 0.05). Ridge is preferred for clinical deployment based on lower parameter variance, near-zero bias, and superior computational simplicity, not an exaggerated accuracy claim.

residual_and_conformal_diagnostics.autocorrelation_status: Near 2.0 (no significant first-order serial correlation in residuals)
residual_and_conformal_diagnostics.surge_coverage_disclosure: Under severe tail surges (>85th percentile), empirical coverage dips because upper-bound volatility exceeds symmetric interval bounds, motivating our two-stage stochastic scenario optimization.
